newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Pirates raid Greek trawler off Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: Pirates raid Greek trawler off Sierra Leone.

text.p: Hooded pirates firing AK-47 automatic rifles attacked a Greek fishing boat off Sierra Leone, wounding some crew, police and crew members said on Saturday.
In the latest incident in growing piracy off the West African country, 11 pirates, most wearing army fatigues, fired on the Alex 3 at close range before boarding it on Thursday night.
"It was a terrible night," recalled the trawler's Greek captain, Nicholas Makaronis after the crew were brought ashore from the scene, 20 nautical miles off the capital Freetown.
"I sounded the alarm as soon as I saw them. But they were fast and furious and in full control of the boat even before my crew knew what was happening," he told reporters.
Makaronis said he was clubbed to the ground with rifle butts and robbed of a gold chain and watch. The pirates also stole fish and shrimps valued at thousands of dollars.
"There were 11 of them, I counted them all," recalled Nats Roberts, another crew member. "They were all wearing black hoods maybe because eight of them were in military fatigues."

Four wounded crew have been admitted in Freetown's Connaught Hospital. Police assembled other crew on Friday for an identity parade of soldiers and civilians rounded up in a raid on a suspected pirates den in the capital's Eastend district.
Sierra Leone government soldiers have been linked to attacks at sea and on highways.
The Alex 3's owner, Likogous Makaronis, who was on the vessel when the pirates struck, told reporters he may have to stop fishing in Sierra Leone's coastal waters.
"I will remove all my boats from the country if stern action is not taken to address piracy," he said.

Trawler owners from Spain, Portugal and West African nations have warned Sierra Leone that piracy could cripple its fishing industry, the only sector operating. Much of the predominantly mining economy has been wrecked by a five-year-old civil war.

About 1,500 fish workers staged a 10-day strike late last month to put pressure on the government to act against piracy. They called off the action on October 1 after the navy seized five soldiers in a crackdown on sea banditry.
